From: Elena Park <elena@harbortech.ai>

Cc: HarborTech Procurement <procurement@harbortech.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning request - Q4 burst and baseline guarantees

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We ran a quick internal sizing exercise and expect two distinct load profiles next fiscal year: a steady baseline (~150 rps of short chat calls) and a sharp mid-quarter burst window for model retraining & heavy inference (estimated 400-600 rps peaks for ~48 hour windows).

Procurement asked for three proposal options we can take to legal: (1) conservative baseline reservation with a small burst pool, (2) tiered reserve that ramps across quarters, and (3) a high-commitment discount with scheduled activation windows. Key constraints: data residency in us-east, ability to pin model versions, and regulatory audit logs.

Can you outline cluster sizing, minimum GPUs per month, and an activation/ramp schedule (we prefer month-by-month tranches rather than one big commit)? Also attach a sample MAP and any SLA language.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, HarborTech

---

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@harbortech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity planning request - tiered reserve structure + options matrix

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity on the two-mode workload. Attached is a concise options matrix plus a recommended "tiered reserve" approach we think balances cost and availability:

Summary (high level)
- Baseline lane: 24 H100 GPUs reserved (steady throughput target; supports ~200 concurrent short-chat rps with batching and KV caching). Always-on.
- Warm reserve: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (lower-cost instances) kept in warm standby; can be spun into production within 2-4 hours for modest bursts.
- Burst pool: 16 H100s available as pre-approved burst credit – billed at burst rate but guaranteed priority during activation windows (48-hour bursts).
- Minimum monthly guarantee (billing): baseline + 25% of burst pool billed as minimum for months in ramp window; pro-rated activation in month of first turn-up.

Ramp schedule (proposed quarter-by-quarter tranches)
- Month 0 (kickoff): Baseline active (24 GPUs), warm reserve hardware pre-provisioned but cold; onboarding & canary tests.
- Month 1: Add 8 GPUs (warm reserve -> active) = 32 active.
- Month 3: Enable first burst tranche (8 of 16 burst GPUs) for scheduled test event.
- Month 6: Full burst pool (16 GPUs) available for unrestricted activation per MAP.

Technical notes
- Preferred SKUs: H100 for baseline/burst heavy-latency workloads; A100P-equivalent for warm reserve to save cost during standby.
- Model pinning: we support pinned model versions and can snapshot KV caches during rollouts (helps steady latency).
- Observability: per-route token-level latency and cost dashboards, plus audit log export to S3 for regulatory needs.

Commercial highlights
- Tiered discount: deeper effective per-token rate for customers who commit to >9 months baseline.
- Early termination: 60-day notice with pro-rated refund for unused months (standard commercial).

Attached: HT-Quote-v2.pdf (line-item pricing), MAP_HarborTech.xlsx (mutual action plan), SLA_Draft.docx (SLA baseline).

Next steps — would you prefer a 12-month staged ramp (we can lock pricing) or a 6-month trial-first cadence? We can also add a "pause/resume" crediting clause for burst credits you don't use.

Thanks,
Rohan
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
